text: ← All problemsStrict convexity of the level-two Gamma-ratio curveLet $\Gamma$ be the Euler Gamma function. For each $x>0$, let $h(x)>0$ be the unique solution of $\frac{\Gamma(h(x))\Gamma(h(x)+2x)}{\Gamma(h(x)+x)^2}=2.$ Is $h$ strictly convex on the whole interval $(0,\infty)$? Explicitly, for distinct $x_0,x_1>0$ and $0<\lambda<1$, must $h(\lambda x_0+(1-\lambda)x_1)<\lambda h(x_0)+(1-\lambda)h(x_1)?$ This is the question in Garrappa–Gerhold–Popolizio–Simon, Remark 16(a), with $h$ defined in Lemma 15. The source establishes strict convexity on $[1,\infty)$. This record concerns the shape of that Gamma-ratio curve, not the separate complete-Bernstein-function and reverse Mittag–Leffler inequality conjectures.ReferencesR. Garrappa, S. Gerhold, M. Popolizio and T. Simon, On some inequalities for the two-parameter Mittag–Leffler function in the complex plane, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 551 (2025), 129588.
